{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOU4GkE88AAAABZRge6g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlaE0zhC4uIE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlaE0", "number": 46, "title": "Add a local-AI simulated livestream demo with camera, speech recognition, and viewer chat", "body": "## Goal

Add a new standalone sandbox demo that lets a person **feel like a livestreamer on a YouTube-inspired video page**: turn on their camera and microphone, see themselves in a large video player, and watch **fictional AI viewer comments** appear from time to time in response to what they say.

**This is a local livestream simulation, not a real stream to the internet.** No actual audience, upload, account, chat backend, or external inference service is needed.

Proposed directory: `projects/ai-livestream/` (name may be adjusted for consistency).

## User experience

- [ ] Open the project to a polished, recognizable **video-streaming watch page** with a large 16:9 video area, a compact stream title/channel area, familiar like/subscribe-style buttons, and a live-chat/comment area.
- [ ] Have **one clear primary action** such as `Go live` / `Start`. Only after a user gesture, request camera + microphone permissions via `getUserMedia`.
- [ ] Show the user's camera feed in the video player (muted locally to prevent audio feedback); provide a clear `End` / stop action that releases camera and microphone tracks.
- [ ] Capture the microphone audio for **on-device speech recognition**. Support spoken **Japanese** (and English if practical), not only English. Do not require typing or manual comment triggering.
- [ ] Use the transcription as context for an **on-device language model** to produce short, natural, varied fictional viewer comments relevant to what was just said. Generate periodically / in small bursts, not one comment per word or a continuous flood.
- [ ] Comments appear with subtle chat-style entrance behavior, believable pseudonyms, and a manageable scrolling history. Keep generation responsive and avoid repetition, irrelevant generic spam, and overly verbose AI replies.
- [ ] Like/subscribe controls should feel interactive but clearly be **local demo UI state**. Do not imply real engagement, real subscribers, or real viewers. Identify the chat as AI/simulated somewhere discoverable without turning the screen into a technical explanation.
- [ ] Allow a short silence without inventing statements that the user did not make. When nothing has been recognized, do not pretend the model heard content.
- [ ] Handle permission denied, missing camera/microphone, unsupported browser/device, model download failure, or low-performance hardware gracefully. Keep the UI simple and retryable.

## Local AI / privacy architecture

- [ ] **Run speech recognition and comment generation entirely in the user's browser.** Consider established browser-local runtimes (e.g., Transformers.js/ONNX Runtime Web and compact Whisper-family ASR, plus an appropriately small local text-generation model with WebGPU or WebAssembly backend), choosing versions and models based on actual browser support, resource requirements and licensing.
- [ ] Use WebGPU acceleration when available; a WebAssembly/CPU fallback is welcome **only where usable**, with honest unsupported-device messaging otherwise. Never silently substitute a paid/remote model API.
- [ ] Keep inference off the main UI thread (e.g., a Worker) when appropriate. Implement bounded audio buffers, cancellation, backpressure, generation cadence, and memory use to avoid runaway CPU/GPU or frozen UI.
- [ ] Load substantial model files **only after the user starts/consents**. Initial model weight downloads/cache are acceptable if required, but inference must not send speech, audio, video, transcripts or prompts to a server. Make first-time downloading/loading progress minimally understandable.
- [ ] Do not record, upload, save, or transmit the camera feed, microphone audio, transcripts, or generated chat to the sandbox backend. Avoid analytics and persistent transcript/history storage; release media resources on stop/unload.
- [ ] Do not add Cloudflare Workers, WebSockets, Durable Objects, D1, TURN, or any server-side AI pipeline. This should run as a **static GitHub Pages demo** with no inference bills.
- [ ] Any third-party model assets or runtime libraries must come from reputable sources, have compatible licenses, and be version-pinned; document model names, weight sizes/rough download implications, and caching/privacy behavior in the project documentation (not as on-screen marketing copy).
- [ ] Clearly acknowledge in docs that performance depends on GPU/CPU, browser and device. Prefer a usable compact model to a large model that only works on high-end hardware.
- [ ] Prevent unsafe/inappropriate personal comments to the extent feasible with local prompting/guardrails; avoid claiming that generated comments reflect a real audience or genuine opinions.

## Visual direction — minimal but premium

**Critical: minimize explanatory copy.** Prior Sandbox demos have sometimes accumulated too many paragraphs, subtitles, small secondary labels, developer terms and helper instructions. For this demo, the visual hierarchy must carry the experience.

- [ ] Use a clean, contemporary **YouTube-inspired** layout, but **do not copy YouTube's logo, branding or exact proprietary assets**. A neutral original identity is fine.
- [ ] Make the **video player the hero**. Place stream title/channel row and like/subscribe-style actions close to it; on desktop place simulated live chat beside the player, on mobile stack it below.
- [ ] Keep text sparse: short title, concise button names, minimal necessary state/permission/error messages. **No onboarding essay, technology badges, explanatory sections, overlong subtitles, or redundant secondary metadata.**
- [ ] Hide technical details such as WebGPU/WASM backend and model diagnostics from the normal UI; use `?debug=1` if troubleshooting is necessary.
- [ ] Use deliberate spacing, typography, pleasing contrast, subtle transitions and responsive design. Keep it stylish and cohesive with the minimalist Sandbox aesthetic.
- [ ] Support mobile touch targets, keyboard navigation, accessible control names, usable status announcements, and `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Sandbox integration

- [ ] Add an independently loadable `projects/<slug>/index.html` so the existing auto-discovery gallery picks it up without manual registration.
- [ ] **Gallery screenshot generation and local/static preview must never request camera/mic permissions, start model downloads, or trigger inference.** Render an attractive inert player/chat preview until the user explicitly starts.
- [ ] Minimize changes to existing project files / site build and do not regress existing demos.
- [ ] Add brief README/project documentation for the static AI demo, device compatibility, user privacy, and model licensing. Keep documentation detail out of the product UI.

## Automated validation / acceptance criteria

These criteria must be testable by the implementation agent without requiring manual confirmation from the user, external hardware, or third-party production credentials.

1. The sandbox discovers and builds the new demo, including a safe, meaningful screenshot cover without any camera/mic prompt or model initialization.
2. The default view presents a polished, uncluttered 16:9 player, channel/action area and live-chat region on desktop/mobile. No excessive helper text or model/infrastructure jargon appears.
3. Starting and stopping a session correctly requests/releases camera and microphone. Automated browser tests use fake media devices/permission mocks, not the user's real devices.
4. A browser-local ASR pipeline can transcribe fixture audio (including Japanese) with no remote inference calls; text is passed to a browser-local generator, which emits relevant, rate-limited fictional comments. Fixture/model tests may be split into deterministic unit coverage plus a bounded real-model smoke test as practical.
5. AI chat does not appear as though real viewers are connected; like/subscribe actions modify only local UI state.
6. Browser APIs missing, permission denial, downloads failing, no speech, rapid start/stop and limited resources are handled without crashes, leaked media tracks, endless loops, or unbounded work.
7. No camera/mic content, audio, video, transcript or generated comments are sent to application servers; verify network requests are limited to the explicit static page/runtime/model-asset fetches needed for first load.
8. Existing site build, gallery capture, static tests and CI checks still pass.

## Non-goals

No actual livestream upload, real YouTube integration, viewer accounts, multiplayer/shared chat, persistent videos, payments, subscriptions, leaderboards, remote LLM/ASR APIs, or production backend. Do not add new features merely to fill empty screen space.

## Implementation note

Choose a workable balance of local model footprint, transcription latency and comment quality. Real-time UX matters more than using the largest LLM; it is acceptable to batch or debounce recognition and generate a comment occasionally. The core requirement is **actual local speech understanding and locally generated responsive comments**, not a hardcoded comment roulette masquerading as an LLM.", "url": "https://github.com/takahirox/sandbox/issues/46", "created_at": "2026-10-23T02:55:54Z", "state": "OPEN", "repository": "takahirox/sandbox", "labels": ["task"], "priority": null, "status": "In Progress", "is_archived": false}, "context": {}, "resources": {}, "allocation": {}, "instruction": null, "run_id": "1f9f0f51095e4c468da1d04a43f15f0c"}
